title: Greco-Persian Wars
summary: When the Achaemenid Empire marched on Greece, a handful of city-states held the line — from Marathon to the shores of Asia Minor.

stories.title: The Persian Invasion
stories.summary: Darius and Xerxes send the largest army Greece had ever seen — and the Greeks answer at five decisive battles.

events.title: Battle of Marathon
events.body: A Persian expeditionary force landed on the plain of Marathon, northeast of Athens. Outnumbered Athenian hoplites charged across the field and shattered the Persian line, preserving Greek independence in a single afternoon.

events.title: Battle of Thermopylae
events.body: King Leonidas and a small Greek force held the narrow pass at Thermopylae for three days against Xerxes' vast army. They were finally outflanked and killed to the last man, but bought critical time for the rest of Greece to prepare.

events.title: Battle of Salamis
events.body: The Greek fleet, led by Themistocles, lured the Persian navy into the narrow straits off Salamis. In cramped waters the lighter Greek triremes outmanoeuvred the larger Persian ships, destroying Xerxes' hope of a quick conquest.

events.title: Battle of Plataea
events.body: A united Greek army under Pausanias confronted the Persian force still occupying Greece. After days of skirmishing, the hoplites broke through the Persian infantry and cavalry, ending the land invasion for good.

events.title: Battle of Mycale
events.body: On the same day as Plataea, a Greek fleet landed on the coast of Ionia and routed the Persian army at Mycale. The victory encouraged the Ionian cities to revolt again and marked the end of Persian power in the Aegean.

stories.title: Ionian Revolt
stories.summary: Greek cities in Asia Minor rise against Persian rule — and draw mainland Greece into the conflict.
